models.description:
# Model Summary

This is a purchase probability prediction model built using scikit-learn.

It is part of a Customer Retention & Revenue Optimization System designed to estimate the likelihood of a customer making a purchase based on behavioral and historical features.

The model helps optimize marketing strategies by identifying customers with high purchase intent, enabling better targeting and improved revenue efficiency.

## Usage

```py
import joblib
import pandas as pd

# Load model and preprocessing artifacts
model = joblib.load("purchase_model.joblib")
scaler = joblib.load("purchase_scaler.joblib")
drop_cols = joblib.load("purchase_drop_cols.joblib")

# Preprocess input data
X = X.drop(columns=drop_cols, errors='ignore')
X_scaled = scaler.transform(X)

# Predict purchase probability or class
predictions = model.predict(X_scaled)
probabilities = model.predict_proba(X_scaled)
```
Input shape: (`n_samples`, `n_features`)    
Output:
- Binary classification (purchase / no purchase)
- Probability scores for purchase likelihood

## System

This model is a standalone machine learning model built using scikit-learn.

Inputs:
- Customer behavioral, transactional, and engagement features

Outputs:
- Purchase prediction (binary classification)
- Purchase probability scores

It can be used directly for marketing targeting and revenue optimization without additional system dependencies.

# Data Overview

The model was trained on structured customer data including:
- Historical purchase behavior
- Engagement and interaction metrics
- Customer attributes and activity patterns

Preprocessing steps included:
- Feature scaling using StandardScaler
- Feature selection using domain-based and statistical filtering
- Removal of irrelevant or redundant columns

# Evaluation Results

The model was evaluated using classification metrics including:
- Accuracy
- Precision
- Recall
- F1-score
- ROC-AUC

A train-test split validation strategy was used to assess generalization performance.

The model is optimized for identifying high-intent customers to improve marketing ROI and revenue targeting efficiency.

# Full Project Repository

The complete implementation, notebooks, source code, models, dashboards, and documentation are available in the GitHub repository.

Full Project Repo: [Customer Retention & Revenue Optimization System](https://github.com/nibeditans/Customer-Retention-Revenue-Optimization-System)

Also check out the detailed project walkthrough: [How to Identify High-Value Customers and Maximize Revenue with Data Science?](https://ai.plainenglish.io/how-to-identify-high-value-customers-and-maximize-revenue-with-data-science-110f77446c6b)

# Model Summary

This is a customer churn prediction model built using scikit-learn.

It is part of a Customer Retention & Revenue Optimization System designed to identify customers likely to churn based on behavioral and transactional features.

The model helps businesses improve retention strategies by proactively targeting high-risk customers.

## Usage

```py
import joblib
import pandas as pd

# Load model and scaler
model = joblib.load("churn_model.joblib")
scaler = joblib.load("churn_scaler.joblib")

# Example input format
# X should match training feature structure
X_scaled = scaler.transform(X)

# Predict churn probability or class
predictions = model.predict(X_scaled)
```
Input shape: (`n_samples`, `n_features`)    
Output: Binary classification (0 = Not churn, 1 = Churn)

## System

This model is a standalone machine learning model built using scikit-learn.

Inputs:
- Customer behavioral and demographic features

Outputs:
- Churn prediction (binary classification)

No external system dependencies required for inference beyond preprocessing.

# Data Overview

The model was trained on structured customer behavioral data including:
- Purchase history
- Engagement metrics
- Customer attributes

Standard preprocessing was applied:
- Feature scaling using StandardScaler
- Handling of missing values
- Feature selection based on importance

# Evaluation Results

The model was evaluated using standard classification metrics:
- Accuracy
- Precision
- Recall
- F1-score

Performance was validated using train-test split methodology.

The model shows strong performance in identifying high-risk churn customers.

# Full Project Repository

The complete implementation, notebooks, source code, models, dashboards, and documentation are available in the GitHub repository.

Full Project Repo: [Customer Retention & Revenue Optimization System](https://github.com/nibeditans/Customer-Retention-Revenue-Optimization-System)

# sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2

This is a [sentence-transformers](https://www.SBERT.net) model: It maps sentences & paragraphs to a 384 dimensional dense vector space and can be used for tasks like clustering or semantic search.



## Usage (Sentence-Transformers)

Using this model becomes easy when you have [sentence-transformers](https://www.SBERT.net) installed:

```
pip install -U sentence-transformers
```

Then you can use the model like this:

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
sentences = ["This is an example sentence", "Each sentence is converted"]

model = SentenceTransformer('sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2')
embeddings = model.encode(sentences)
print(embeddings)
```



## Usage (HuggingFace Transformers)
Without [sentence-transformers](https://www.SBERT.net), you can use the model like this: First, you pass your input through the transformer model, then you have to apply the right pooling-operation on-top of the contextualized word embeddings.

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
import torch


#Mean Pooling - Take attention mask into account for correct averaging
def mean_pooling(model_output, attention_mask):
    token_embeddings = model_output[0] #First element of model_output contains all token embeddings
    input_mask_expanded = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand(token_embeddings.size()).float()
    return torch.sum(token_embeddings * input_mask_expanded, 1) / torch.clamp(input_mask_expanded.sum(1), min=1e-9)


# Sentences we want sentence embeddings for
sentences = ['This is an example sentence', 'Each sentence is converted']

# Load model from HuggingFace Hub
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/paraphrase-MiniLM-L3-v2')

# Tokenize sentences
encoded_input = tokenizer(sentences, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt')

# Compute token embeddings
with torch.no_grad():
    model_output = model(**encoded_input)

# Perform pooling. In this case, max pooling.
sentence_embeddings = mean_pooling(model_output, encoded_input['attention_mask'])

print("Sentence embeddings:")
print(sentence_embeddings)
```



## Full Model Architecture
```
SentenceTransformer(
  (0): Transformer({'max_seq_length': 128, 'do_lower_case': False}) with Transformer model: BertModel 
  (1): Pooling({'word_embedding_dimension': 384, 'pooling_mode_cls_token': False, 'pooling_mode_mean_tokens': True, 'pooling_mode_max_tokens': False, 'pooling_mode_mean_sqrt_len_tokens': False})
)
```

## Citing & Authors

This model was trained by [sentence-transformers](https://www.sbert.net/). 
        
If you find this model helpful, feel free to cite our publication [Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084):
```bibtex 
@inproceedings{reimers-2019-sentence-bert,
    title = "Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks",
    author = "Reimers, Nils and Gurevych, Iryna",
    booktitle = "Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing",
    month = "11",
    year = "2019",
    publisher = "Association for Computational Linguistics",
    url = "http://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084",
}
```

# Model Summary

This model predicts student academic performance using study habits and lifestyle-related factors such as study hours, sleep duration, stress level, and attendance. The model was developed using Scikit-learn and trained on the “Study Habits and Performance” dataset for educational and beginner-level machine learning purposes.

## Usage

The model can be used to predict student marks based on input features including Study_hours, Sleep_hours, Stress_level, and Attendance.

```python
import pandas as pd
import joblib

model = joblib.load("student_performance_model.pkl")

sample = pd.DataFrame({
    "Study_hours": [4],
    "Sleep_hours": [7],
    "Stress_level": [3],
    "Attendance": [90]
})

prediction = model.predict(sample)
print(prediction)
```

Input Shape: (n_samples, 4)
Output Shape: (n_samples, 1)

## System

This is a standalone regression model developed using Scikit-learn. The model requires numerical input values for study hours, sleep hours, stress level, and attendance percentage.

## Implementation requirements

Training and inference were performed using Python, pandas, scikit-learn, and joblib on a standard CPU-based environment. No GPU or high-performance hardware was required.

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

The model was trained from scratch using structured tabular educational data.

## Model stats

The model is lightweight, CPU-efficient, and suitable for beginner-level machine learning applications with low inference latency.

## Other details

The model is not pruned or quantized, and no differential privacy techniques were applied.

# Data Overview

The model was trained using the “Study Habits and Performance” dataset containing synthetic educational data focused on student lifestyle and academic behavior.

## Training data

The dataset includes the following features:

* Study_hours
* Sleep_hours
* Stress_level
* Attendance
* Marks

The data was manually curated and preprocessed through validation and cleaning steps to ensure consistency and realistic value ranges.

## Demographic groups

The dataset does not include demographic or sensitive personal attributes such as gender, ethnicity, religion, or age.

## Evaluation data

The dataset was split into training and testing sets using an 80:20 ratio for model evaluation.

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

The model demonstrates the relationship between study habits and academic performance and provides beginner-level regression predictions on structured educational data.

## Subgroup evaluation results

No subgroup analysis was performed because the dataset does not contain demographic information.

## Fairness

No fairness-specific evaluation metrics were applied since the dataset excludes sensitive demographic attributes.

## Usage limitations

This model is intended for educational, research, and learning purposes only and should not be used for real academic decision-making.

## Ethics

The model was developed using synthetic data to avoid privacy concerns and ensure safe public educational use.
